root_cause.text: In `net/rose/af_rose.c`, `rose_kill_by_device()` iterates over a locally collected socket pointer array but uses the wrong index (`array[cnt]` instead of `array[i]`), causing an uninitialized or out-of-bounds read and possible invalid socket dereference/reference leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `sk = array[cnt];` to `sk = array[i];`, and the CVE/commit message states that `array[cnt]` “reads an uninitialized entry; for cnt == ARRAY_SIZE(array), it is an out-of-bounds read,” which can dereference an invalid socket pointer and leak `sock_hold()` references.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the socket iteration in rose_kill_by_device() to use the loop index when killing sockets by device.
intent_record.what: In the loop inside rose_kill_by_device(), the assignment changed from `sk = array[cnt];` to `sk = array[i];`.
intent_record.how: This makes the loop iterate over the collected socket array correctly by using the current index instead of the total count, preventing repeated access to the same out-of-bounds or wrong element and allowing each socket to be processed and removed as intended.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the socket iteration in rose_kill_by_device() to use the loop index when killing sockets by device.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes rose_kill_by_device() socket iteration to use the correct loop index instead of the wrong array element, addressing the out-of-bounds/uninitialized read and invalid socket access.

candidates.rationale: This uses the total count as the array index inside the loop, so it reads past the intended element range and can dereference an uninitialized or out-of-bounds socket pointer instead of the current entry.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement uses the total socket count as the array index inside the iteration, instead of the loop index. That causes an out-of-bounds or uninitialized read from the local socket pointer array in rose_kill_by_device(), which can lead to invalid socket dereference or reference leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable pattern is present in the shown function body: in the post-collection loop it does `for (i = 0; i < cnt; i++) { sk = array[cnt]; ... }` which uses `cnt` instead of the loop index `i`. This is the exact wrong-index bug described in the root cause, leading to an out-of-bounds/uninitialized read of `array[cnt]` when `cnt` equals the number of collected sockets. The later added locking/refcount changes (`lock_sock(sk); spin_lock_bh(&rose_list_lock); ... sock_put(sk);`) are not a fix for this indexing mistake, and the snippet does not show any correction such as `array[i]`.
